subtitle: Lesson 27 · Honeypots & Deception Technology

eyebrow: A honeypot is one example, not the idea

steps.label: Honeypot
steps.sub: one decoy system — catches only who finds it

steps.label: Deception tech
steps.sub: the whole category, planted throughout the environment

steps.label: More tripwires
steps.sub: more chances to catch lateral movement

code:
config.yml:
  aws_access_key = "AKIA-FAKE-HONEYTOKEN"   <- never used legitimately

ALERT fires the instant this key is used anywhere
caption: A fake credential or file planted so that its use is unambiguous evidence of compromise.

steps.label: Fake AD account
steps.sub: looks privileged, no real admin ever uses it

steps.label: Fake group
steps.sub: catches reconnaissance against the directory itself

code:
Attacker compromises workstation via phishing
  -> reads config.yml       (honeytoken alert)
  -> enumerates AD groups   (decoy account alert)
  -> browses shares         (decoy share alert)

3 tripwires, near-certain confirmation within minutes
caption: Any one tripwire would be enough — layered decoys confirm compromise almost immediately.

subtitle: The low false-positive rate that makes deception worth it.
